references.text: God instructed Moses to speak to Aaron and put the words in his mouth, which Moses now does by telling Aaron all the Lord's words.
Describes the signs God gave Moses—the staff turning into a snake, the hand becoming leprous, and water turning into blood—which Moses now tells Aaron about.
The Lord's words that Moses was sent with to the elders of Israel, which he now conveys to Aaron.
Moses and Aaron later perform the signs before Pharaoh, which Moses first told Aaron about.
Aaron speaks all the words the Lord had spoken to Moses and performs the signs before the people—a direct fulfillment of what Moses told him.
Parallel in the communication process: Moses transfers 'all the Lord's words' first to Aaron (leadership) and later to the entire people (covenant).
Direct narrative connection: The delivery of the mission concerning the signs (4:28) is followed by their performance (7:6).
